text:
Noah: heads-up reproducible weirdness during a canary: long-lived cursor + prefetch+soft-evict => stale reads and a persistent pin leak. wrote steps below.
Priya: that sounds nasty. TL;DR of repro?
Noah: sequence: (1) tenant T opens long cursor C and triggers prefetch for prefix P (pins entries in slab). (2) autoscaler moves P to node B via soft-handoff; A demotes but keeps pinned entries around because of cursor pin. (3) later writes land on B and become authoritative; reads routed round-robin hit A and get old values because A's pinned slab wasn't invalidated on demote.
Ethan: isn't pin supposed to be soft and dropped on demote? I thought demote unpinned prefixes after grace window.
Noah: it does for ordinary pins, but cursor pins are treated as livelock-protected and only released when cursor closes or times out. long cursors (minutes) plus prefetch means pins stick around much longer than handoff windows.
Miriam: two issues then: correctness (A serving stale pinned values) and accounting (pins never released -> memory leak).
Priya: can we treat cursor-pins differently: convert prefetch cursors to shadow-pins that are invalidated on demote (read-only) rather than strong pins?
Ethan: maybe but app code relies on cursors for snapshot-consistent scans; shadow-pins might break semantics if the cursor expects a stable snapshot.
Noah: idea: keep cursor semantics but add visibility generation per-entry. On demote we bump prefix.visibility_gen and mark pinned entries as "stale-if-gen<mismatch". Cursor reads that detect mismatch either re-sync from authoritative or advance snapshot to include later LSNs.
Miriam: per-entry gen sounds heavy. Could we track per-prefix gen and attach gen to each pinned slab-list: pin.gen = prefix.gen_at_pin_time. On read: if pin.gen != prefix.gen then invalidate pin and fetch from authoritative. cheap compare.
Priya: that avoids per-entry writes. But how do we handle snapshot cursors that expect earlier values? If we invalidate, cursor might see gaps compared to its snapshot.
Noah: good point. Two snapshot options: (A) cursors are allowed to serve a slightly older snapshot only while pinned locally; after takeover we surface an explicit cursor-invalidated error so clients can reopen snapshot. (B) we implement transfer-of-pin: during handoff, current owner can serialize pinned state to B so cursors continue seamlessly.
Ethan: (B) is complex and requires shipping slab entries or references over network, plus backpressure on big cursors. (A) seems simpler: invalidate cursors on handoff and require client retry. Most of our long-lived cursors are internal streamer clients that can handle retry. Need to check customer impact.
Miriam: operationally we also need to avoid pin leaks: demote should force-release cursor pins after X ms and emit metric 'prefix.cursor_pin_forced_release'. Also alert if leaked memory > threshold.
Priya: propose combined approach: 1) prefix.cursor_pin_mode = {transferable, invalidated}. Default is invalidated. 2) when handoff starts, bump prefix.gen++; owner sets prefix.handoff_in_progress tag. 3) readers that encounter pin with pin.gen != prefix.gen return CURSOR_INVALIDATED (client visible) and trigger pin release. 4) optional experimental transferable mode where during canary we attempt to migrate pin metadata via streaming, with explicit max bytes limit.
Noah: add flags and metrics: runtime.flags.cursor_pin_invalidation=true, runtime.flags.cursor_pin_transfer=true (canary only). metrics: prefix.cursor_invalidations, prefix.cursor_transfer_bytes.
Ethan: add a devtest that creates N long cursors, fuzz handoffs, and assert no stale reads and no sustained memory growth. Also simulate transfer failures and ensure clients see CURSOR_INVALIDATED and can retry cleanly.
Miriam: qa-bot: create test-ticket?
qa-bot: created TEST-2481: "cursor pin handoff fuzz + regression" assigned to @ethan and @miriam, due 2026-04-12 :white_check_mark:
Priya: also update docs about semantics: cursors are not guaranteed to survive ownership change unless transferable mode is enabled. We should notify internal customers and add an FAQ.
Noah: good. I'll prototype prefix.gen + pin.gen delta and forced release logic. ETA initial spike + microbench next week.
Priya: sgtm. thanks. keep notes in the RFC follow-up doc.
Miriam: :thumbsup:
